milestone.title: [tests] Stop linking jsonschema into all 124 test binaries

intent.outcome: After this ships, default cargo test no longer links jsonschema + its 30-crate tree into mp test binaries (oracle split). make dep-audit drops well below 110 (achieved 137→56). Cold wall-clock one-minute drop was not achieved (entry 27); incremental re-link is the intended win axis and awaits measured threshold pin.

problem.description: `crates/mp/Cargo.toml` (pre-M161) declared `jsonschema = 0.46.5` as a `[dev-dependency]` of `mp`. Even though only 2 test files used it (then at `tests/suites/mini_schema_parity.rs` and `tests/suites/mini_schema_e2e.rs`, now at `crates/mp-oracle/tests/`), the dep was linked into every one of the 68 (at M161) / 69 (after M162) integration test binaries that depend on `mp`. Cargo's incremental cache helps when nothing changed, but a single edit to `crates/mp/src/` triggered re-link of all binaries -- each paying for ~30 transitive crates (visible in `target/debug/deps/` as ~17K .d files). This was the single largest cold-build cost.

in_scope: Move `jsonschema` out of `[dev-dependencies]` in `crates/mp/Cargo.toml` into a new minimal workspace member `crates/mp-oracle/` with its own `Cargo.toml` listing only `jsonschema` + `mp` as deps.
Move `crates/mp/tests/suites/mini_schema_parity.rs` and `crates/mp/tests/suites/mini_schema_e2e.rs` under `crates/mp-oracle/tests/` (or expose a thin shim that re-exports the assertions).
Document the oracle boundary in `crates/mp-oracle/README.md` — why it exists, when to add tests to it vs `mp/`.
out_of_scope: No change to `mp`'s runtime path (jsonschema is dev-only today; stays dev-only).
No change to `mini_schema.rs` source (still the runtime validator).
No change to other dev-deps (tempfile, libc stay where they are).
No change to CI gating — oracle tests still run on every PR, just from a separate workspace member.

findings.description: crates/mp-oracle/tests/common/mod.rs::mp_bin() resolves target/debug/mp at runtime without the hardlink-snapshot retry that crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs::mp_bin() uses (M132). If a parallel cargo rebuild clobbers target/debug/mp while the oracle suite is running, mp_oracle's 2 test binaries could spawn-fail with ENOENT. Mitigation: lift the snapshot helpers from crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs into mp-oracle. Verdict: low blast radius — mp-oracle's 2 tests do not trigger mp rebuilds and run in their own cargo test binary, so the race is unlikely in practice. Leave for external review to confirm or close.
findings.fixed_in: Closed as wontfix after independent verification: reproduced the race by running cargo build -p mp --bin mp concurrently with cargo nextest run -p mp-oracle (including after touch crates/mp/src/lib.rs to force a real rebuild). All 9 mp-oracle tests passed in every run. Blast radius is bounded: mp-oracle's 2 tests do not trigger mp rebuilds (they only link against mp's lib), run in their own cargo test binary separate from the 122 mp test binaries, and target/debug/mp is owned by cargo's atomic-rename pattern. README and tests/common/mod.rs both call out the fallback path, so debt is documented and closure criterion is clear. Not worth ~80 LOC of copy-paste today.

findings.description: crates/mp-oracle/Cargo.toml says "Intentionally NO [lib] — this crate is test-only" but src/lib.rs exists, so cargo auto-detects a lib target (verified via cargo metadata: targets include "lib - mp_oracle"). The comment is misleading: cargo does compile a library (named mp_oracle); the lib just has no public API. Suggested fix: clarify the comment to say "this crate has no public lib API — tests live under tests/; the lib stub is required because cargo integration tests under tests/ must link against a crate lib."
findings.fixed_in: Fixed in crates/mp-oracle/Cargo.toml: rewrote the misleading 'Intentionally NO [lib]' comment. The new text says 'This crate is test-only by intent — it has NO public lib API.' and explains that cargo still compiles a lib target because integration tests under tests/ must link against a crate lib. Verified with cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 — mp-oracle's targets are lib + 2 tests as before, no behavior change.

findings.description: crates/mp-oracle/README.md 'When to add a test to mp-oracle' rules don't fit the e2e test (crates/mp-oracle/tests/mini_schema_e2e.rs): that test does NOT import jsonschema and is NOT a parity check between mp's runtime validator and an external canonical implementation. It is an end-to-end test of mp's schema-enforcement path. Step S2-MOVE-E2E justifies the move as 'keeps AC-02 honest about the 2-test oracle boundary', but the README rule list omits this case. Suggested fix: add a bullet like 'the test is an end-to-end check of mp's schema-enforcement path (CLI spawn + exit-code assertion)' so future contributors know e2e schema tests belong here even when they don't import jsonschema.
findings.fixed_in: Fixed in crates/mp-oracle/README.md: added a third bullet to 'When to add a test to mp-oracle' that explicitly covers end-to-end schema-enforcement tests (CLI spawn + exit-code assertion). This matches the rationale in step S2-MOVE-E2E: 'keeps AC-02 honest about the 2-test oracle boundary' — the e2e test pairs with the parity tests in CI even though it doesn't import jsonschema.

findings.description: crates/mp-oracle/src/lib.rs comment 'this lib stub is required by cargo even though it has no logic' is misleading — the allow(dead_code) attribute has nothing to do with 'stub' status. The crate root has no items to lint (no functions, no use statements), so the allow is purely defensive. Suggested fix: rewrite the comment to say 'Defensive: keep this lib stub free of items so adding a stray import doesn't get an unused warning; integration tests under tests/ link against this lib.' Or remove the allow if no longer needed.
findings.fixed_in: Fixed in crates/mp-oracle/src/lib.rs: rewrote the misleading 'this lib stub is required by cargo even though it has no logic' comment to clarify that dead_code is a defensive lint-suppression (the stub has no items to lint today; the allow keeps a stray future import from producing an unused warning). Kept the attribute since it's harmless and prevents future regression.

findings.description:
The '122 test binaries' / '122 binaries' claim is repeated in 4 new M161-owned files plus the inherited milestone intent and mp-dogfood-log.md Entry 27:

- crates/mp-oracle/Cargo.toml:6 (description)
- crates/mp-oracle/README.md:5 (the 122 integration-test binaries in crates/mp/tests/)
- crates/mp-oracle/README.md:21 (every of the ~122 integration-test binaries)
- crates/mp-oracle/src/lib.rs:5 (the 122 integration-test binaries)
- crates/mp/Cargo.toml:30 comment (every mp test binary)
- master-plan/milestones/161-*.json intent.outcome (the 122 test binaries)
- mp-dogfood-log.md Entry 27 (122 test binaries re-link the 30-crate tree)

Empirical count at commit d08823a (M161): git ls-tree -r crates/mp/tests/ --name-only | grep .rs | grep -v suites/ | grep -v common/ = 68 test binaries. After M162 (6939860) added lib_api_parity.rs: 69.

So 122 is wrong by ~80 (1.8x too high). Either the original spec used a different counting convention (counting suite modules?) or it was an off-by-2x authoring error that propagated through the spec → intent → commit message → new crate's README/lib.rs/Cargo.toml → dogfood log. Future readers comparing the documented claim against cargo metadata (which reports 69 lib.test targets today) will see the discrepancy.

Fix: replace '122' with the actual count in the 4 M161-owned files, and note in the dogfood log that the original 122 was off. The intent.outcome is the source of truth — recommend an mp milestone update to reflect the corrected count (this is also a spec-gap). Verification: cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | jq '[.packages[] | select(.name == "mp") | .targets[] | select(.kind == ["test"])] | length' should match the corrected count.
findings.summary: M161 docs claim 122 test binaries but actual mp test count is 68 at M161 time (69 after M162)

findings.description:
crates/mp-oracle/tests/mini_schema_parity.rs:138-153 builds a multi-line json!() and binds it to 'valid', then immediately does 'let _ = valid; // placeholder; real milestone schema is exercised via the suite' on line 153. The comment admits it's a placeholder that was never wired up. The two assert_agree calls below exercise only schema.clone() against json!({}) and json!({'milestone': {}}).

This dead code pre-existed in crates/mp/tests/suites/mini_schema_parity.rs (verified via git show d08823a~1:...) — M125-era code authored it. M161 moved the file as-is to crates/mp-oracle/tests/ without cleaning up. So the dead block traveled with the move.

Two reasonable fixes:
(a) Wire up the valid instance: change the 'let _ = valid' to 'assert_agree(schema.clone(), valid)' so the test actually exercises the milestone schema's accept-the-valid-envelope case (currently the test only checks both validators reject empty + nested-empty).
(b) Delete lines 138-153 entirely since the test name is 'parity_milestone_valid_and_mutations' but only mutation cases (rejects) are exercised — the 'valid' half of the name is a lie today.

Either fix is one-line and makes the test live up to its name. Low severity because the test still passes and the other 6 parity tests cover the actual validator contract.
findings.summary: Dead 'valid' json!() in mini_schema_parity.rs::parity_milestone_valid_and_mutations carried through M161 move

findings.description:
POSIX text-file convention is to end with a newline. The new M161-owned files break this convention:

- crates/mp-oracle/Cargo.toml: ends with '}' (no final \n)
- crates/mp-oracle/README.md: ends with 'crates/mp/src/mini_schema.rs` (the runtime validator)' (no final \n)

Verified via tail -c | od -c. The workspace root Cargo.toml, crates/mp/Cargo.toml, and most other text files in the repo end with a final newline. cargo fmt --all -- --check does not catch this because it only operates on Rust source files.

Fix: append a single \n to both files. cargo fmt does not enforce it; a pre-commit or editorconfig check would. Low severity, style only.
findings.summary: crates/mp-oracle/Cargo.toml and README.md missing trailing newline (other workspace files have one)
